title: Impulse and Momentum
learning_goal: Calculate and describe momentum and impulse and connect impulse to changes in momentum.

stages.title: 1. Momentum
stages.content: Linear momentum describes motion and is given by p = mv. Momentum is a vector, so direction matters.

stages.title: 2. Impulse
stages.content: Impulse is the product of force and time interval, J = FΔt, for a constant force. Impulse equals the change in momentum: J = Δp.

stages.title: 3. Worked example
stages.content: A 2 kg ball moving at 6 m/s has momentum p = mv = 12 kg·m/s in its direction of motion.

stages.title: 4. Why contact time matters
stages.content: For the same change in momentum, increasing the collision time reduces the average force. This is why airbags, padding, and crumple zones can reduce injury.

stages.title: 5. Guided practice
stages.prompt: A constant 10 N force acts on an object for 3 s. What impulse is delivered?
stages.alternate_explanation: Impulse measures force acting over time, so multiply the force by how long it acts.

stages.title: 6. Mastery check
stages.content: To demonstrate mastery, calculate p = mv, calculate J = FΔt, use J = Δp, and explain how changing collision time affects force.
